stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Slides with real-time co-editing
stories.summary: In release notes published October 16, OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Slides, a feature for creating and editing presentations inside ChatGPT's shared Space workspace. It is rolling out to eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise users with Space access on the web and desktop app. Users can start a deck from a conversation, files, an outline, or an example deck; edit text, images, shapes, and charts directly; invite teammates to edit in real time with shared comments; present from ChatGPT; and export to PowerPoint, PDF, Google Slides, or Keynote.
facts: Release notes published October 16 introduced ChatGPT Slides for creating and editing presentations in Space.
Rolling out to eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise users with Space access, on the web and in the desktop app.
A deck can start from a conversation, files, an outline, or an example deck.
Users can edit text, images, shapes, and charts directly or ask ChatGPT to make the changes; invited teammates can edit the same deck in real time and leave shared comments.
Presentations run directly in ChatGPT; on the web they export to PowerPoint, PDF, or Google Slides, and in the desktop app they open in PowerPoint or Keynote when those apps are installed.
OpenAI also updated GPT-6 Pro in ChatGPT: faster responses, improved plugin and tool use, and multiple agents that can handle parts of a task in parallel — rolling out to eligible Pro users.
Per web-search coverage: Space itself was unveiled at OpenAI's DevDay on September 29, and the rollout is gradual — many users on the right plan may not see Slides yet.

stories.full_text:
OpenAI Adds Slides and Parallel Agents to ChatGPT
In release notes published October 16, OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Slides for creating and editing presentations in Space. The feature is rolling out to eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise users with Space access on the web and desktop app.
Users can start a presentation from a conversation, files, an outline, or an example deck. They can edit text, images, shapes, and charts directly, ask ChatGPT to make changes, invite teammates to edit in real time, and leave shared comments.
Presentations can run directly in ChatGPT. Web users can export them to PowerPoint, PDF, or Google Slides, while desktop users can open decks in PowerPoint or Keynote when those applications are installed.
OpenAI also updated GPT-6 Pro in ChatGPT with faster responses, improved plugin and tool use, and multiple agents that can handle parts of a task in parallel. The update is rolling out to eligible Pro users, while access in managed workspaces depends on workspace settings and rollout eligibility.

stories.title: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017 with MIT open weights and search APIs
stories.summary: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17, an update to the V4.1-Flash model it launched in September, live on its website, app, and API under the existing deepseek-flash name. The weights are open-sourced under the MIT licence on Hugging Face and ModelScope. On DeepSeek's own comparison the checkpoint scores 77.0 on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark, ahead of Claude Opus 5's 74.0. Separately, DeepSeek opened its own Search and Fetch APIs to all developers at $0.75 per 1,000 calls.

stories.full_text:
DeepSeek moves up the stack: V4.1-Flash update ships alongside its own Search and Fetch APIs for agents
What happened? DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17, an update to the V4.1-Flash model it launched in September. It is live on DeepSeek's website, app and API, served under the existing deepseek-flash model name, and the weights are open-sourced under the MIT licence on Hugging Face and ModelScope. DeepSeek calls it "a Pareto improvement in performance and cost": stronger benchmark scores with faster task completion and shorter outputs.
The numbers: On DeepSeek's own comparison, the update scores 77.0 on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark (up from 74.2), ahead of Claude Opus 5 (74.0) and GPT-5.6 Sol (73.0), and leads its table on Automation-Bench, Agents' Last Exam and Apex Bench. Claude Opus 5 still leads on Humanity's Last Exam, Terminal-Bench 4.0, ProgramBench and NL2Repo-Bench. DeepSeek also says the model now builds complete projects end to end, from games to 3D models, using reinforcement learning with self-feedback.
Beyond the model: The bigger shift is infrastructure. DeepSeek opened its Search and Fetch APIs to all developers, powered by an in-house search engine it says serves hundreds of millions of requests a day. Each endpoint costs $0.75 per 1,000 calls; calls made through server-side tools in DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex stay free for DeepSeek API users until per-request billing starts on November 1, 2026, Beijing time. The model is also tuned for DeepSeek's own agent harness, DeepSeek Harness, and for Tencent's CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy. That gives agent builders a low-cost model plus a first-party web search layer behind one API key, putting DeepSeek in competition with dedicated search-API providers for agent workloads.
Context: The release comes as DeepSeek's latest funding round has reportedly grown to between $12 billion and $15 billion at a valuation of about $75 billion, ahead of a planned Shanghai IPO, according to CNBC.
Sources DeepSeek on X, Hugging Face model card, DeepSeek Search & Fetch API docs, MarkTechPost. Chart: DeepSeek.

stories.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops ship from $2,599 with 128GB unified memory
stories.summary: Microsoft opened pre-orders for the Surface Laptop Ultra, its first laptop on NVIDIA's RTX Spark N1X platform, at a $2,599 starting price with shipping beginning October 16. The base config pairs an 18-core NVIDIA N1X CPU with a 5,120-core Blackwell GPU, 24GB of unified memory, and a 512GB SSD; machines can be configured up to 128GB of unified memory ($5,899 top config) aimed at local AI workloads. The launch lands alongside Meta's 816B Muse Spark Open, which Apple demoed running locally on four M5 Ultra Mac Studios at 36.73 tokens per second — sharpening the Windows-vs-Apple local-AI contest.
facts: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599 and begins shipping on October 16.
Base config: 18-core NVIDIA N1X CPU, 5,120-core NVIDIA Blackwell GPU, 24GB unified memory, 512GB SSD.
Configurable up to 128GB of unified memory, with the full SoC (20-core CPU, 6,144-core GPU, 1TB SSD) at $5,899.
15-inch mini-LED HDR touchscreen with up to 2,000 nits peak brightness; about 4.5 pounds; magnetic USB Type-C charging; triple Type-C, USB-A, HDMI, full-size SD reader, 3.5mm headphone jack.
The 128GB unified memory pool is pitched at local AI workloads — running larger models locally instead of relying on cloud services.
Microsoft demonstrated gaming chops: 60 FPS in Gears of War: E-Day.
Price context in article: HP OmniBook X 14 starts at $2,999 (16-inch at $3,199), with higher models reaching $4,499/$4,999.

Per verified web-search coverage: Meta released Muse Spark Open (816B parameters, 42B active) on October 15; Apple's MLX benchmarks ran it at 36.73 tokens/sec on FOUR M5 Ultra Mac Studios and 24.99 tokens/sec on two (tensor mode).
CORRECTION vs the scan summary: the scan said 'two M5 Ultra Mac Studios at 36+ tokens per second' — that is inaccurate; the 36+ tps figure required four machines, per Apple/verified coverage.

Per verified web-search coverage (NVIDIA's own claims, treat with scepticism): RTX Spark delivers up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance; NVIDIA claims up to 2.1x faster time-to-first-token vs a MacBook Pro with M5 Pro — company-supplied figures, not independent benchmarks.
Note: the original scan placeholder https://aibriefing.dev/ was a HOMEPAGE, replaced with this specific article about RTX Spark laptops shipping.
stories.full_text:
Microsoft has unveiled the pricing for the RTX Spark-based Surface laptops and the shipping date.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark Starts at $2,599, Undercutting HP's RTX Spark Laptops
Microsoft has officially opened pre-orders for the Surface Laptop Ultra, its first laptop powered by the newly launched NVIDIA RTX Spark platform. The machine is priced at a starting price of $2,599 and will begin shipping on October 16. This positions it as one of the first premium Windows laptops built around NVIDIA's Arm-based N1X platform.
The base configuration for the laptop features the 18-core NVIDIA N1X CPU coupled with the 5120-core NVIDIA Blackwell GPU. This SoC will be paired with 24 GB of unified memory and a 512 GB SSD as the base configuration. However, users can configure the laptop with up to 128 GB of unified memory, and the full SoC with a 20-core CPU, a 6144-core GPU, and a 1 TB SSD for a whopping $5,899.
The new Surface Laptop Ultra features a 15-inch mini-LED HDR touchscreen with a peak brightness of up to 2,000 nits. The machine reportedly weighs about 4.5 pounds and includes triple Type-C ports, USB-A, HDMI, a full-size SD reader, and a 3.5 mm headphone jack for connectivity. Moreover, it will also introduce magnetic USB Type-C charging instead of the traditional Surface Connect port.
The 128 GB unified memory pool remains its biggest selling point as NVIDIA and Microsoft are targeting local AI workloads. With such a large memory pool, it will be easier for the users to run larger AI models locally rather than relying on the cloud services. Microsoft also demonstrated the laptop's gaming capabilities, promising 60 FPS in titles like Gears of War: E-Day.
As far as pricing is concerned, the $2,599 starting price looks interesting when we compare it against HP's RTX Spark offerings. The HP OmniBook X 14 starts at $2,999, while the larger 16-inch variant will be priced at $3,199. However, the higher HP models reach $4,499 for the OmniBook X 14 and about $4,999 for the OmniBook Ultra 16.
The $400 price gap is surely a significant advantage for Microsoft, although direct comparisons depend on the overall configuration, including memory, storage, and display. We saw HP's laptops bringing more memory onboard, higher storage, and OLED displays capped at 120 Hz. So, that's a major advantage for HP as well.

stories.title: Recruiter catches deepfake job candidate with hand-wave test
stories.summary: Michigan-based recruiter Jason (@loktar00) posted a clip on X on October 16 saying he had just interviewed his 'first deepfake candidate.' After his coworker noticed glitched glasses and a ghosted second frame, Jason asked the candidate to put a hand in front of his face, demonstrating John Cena's 'You Can't See Me' wave himself — and the candidate avoided doing so. The clip went viral, sparking fresh debate over AI misuse in remote hiring.
facts: A recruiter named Jason (Michigan-based, posts as @loktar00) shared the clip on X on October 16, saying he had just interviewed his 'first deepfake candidate.'
Partway through the call he suspected the applicant was using a live digital filter to change his appearance.
His coworker noticed the candidate's glasses looked off and there was 'a second ghost frame smeared across his cheeks.'

Jason asked the candidate to put a hand in front of his face, demonstrating it himself with John Cena's famous 'You Can't See Me' wave; the candidate avoided putting his hand directly in front of his face — enough to raise Jason's suspicions.

Article explains the mechanics: live face-swap/filter tools track a face and lay a digital overlay on it; a hand passing in front can confuse the software, making the image glitch, blur or break apart.

Not the first such case: Dawid Moczadlo, cofounder of Vidoc Security Lab, went viral earlier with footage where a candidate's face kept glitching; when asked to cover his face, the candidate ignored the request and the interview was ended.
A recruiter at the digital studio Make described a similar episode: when she asked a candidate to wave a hand in front of their face, he left the call immediately.
Social media users were largely on Jason's side; he wrote: 'In the days of AI we're going to have to be more careful.. and forced to move to in person interviews.'

Article's own caveat: this is one recruiter's account of one call; the candidate hasn't been identified; avoiding an odd request isn't proof of a deepfake; security firms warn simple checks like the hand wave won't stay reliable as the technology improves.

Note: the X post itself (from @loktar00, Oct 16, with media pic.twitter.com/r2HnbwroMV) is embedded in the article, but its exact x.com status URL could not be recovered — x.com is blocked in this environment, so x_media_url is null rather than a guess.
stories.full_text:
Job interviews have always involved a little performance, but one recruiter says a candidate took it too far. A video making the rounds online shows a recruiter named Jason pausing a remote interview to check whether the person on screen was real, using a gesture borrowed from the wrestling ring.
In a clip shared on X on October 16, Jason says he has just interviewed his "first deepfake candidate." Partway through the call, he suspects the applicant is using a live digital filter to change his appearance. So he asks the candidate to put a hand in front of his face.
To make the request easier, Jason demonstrates it himself, doing John Cena's famous "You Can't See Me" wave. The candidate, according to reports, avoids putting his hand directly in front of his face. That was enough to raise Jason's suspicions.
Live face-swap and filter tools work by tracking a face and laying a digital overlay on top of it. A hand passing in front of the face can confuse the software, making the image glitch, blur or break apart. It's an old trick among recruiters. Jason isn't the first to try it. Dawid Moczadło, cofounder of Vidoc Security Lab, went viral earlier with footage of an interview where the candidate's face kept glitching. When asked to cover his face, the candidate ignored the request, and the interview was ended. A recruiter at the digital studio Make described a similar episode: when she asked a candidate to wave a hand in front of their face, he left the call immediately.
Social media users were largely on Jason's side, praising him for catching the behaviour. Many treated the clip as a sign of the times, with remote hiring now needing a little theatre of its own. He posted the video on X and wrote, “In the days of AI we're going to have to be more careful.. and forced to move to in person interviews.”
It's worth remembering that this is one recruiter's account of one call. The candidate hasn't been identified, and avoiding an odd request isn't proof of a deepfake. Some security firms also warn that simple checks like the hand wave won't stay reliable for long, since the technology keeps improving.

stories.title: AI-generated iPhone shipwreck videos go viral; Al Jazeera debunks them
stories.summary: Videos claiming to show Iranian fishermen retrieving iPhones and perfumes from a sunken cargo ship went viral online, gathering millions of views. An Al Jazeera investigation found the clips were AI-generated. The underlying incident was real — the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sank on October 14 after a fire — but all 21 crew members were rescued safely and none of the viral footage was genuine.
facts: Videos claiming to show Iranian fishermen retrieving iPhones and perfumes from a sunken cargo ship went viral online, reportedly gathering millions of views.
An Al Jazeera investigation found the clips were AI-generated.
The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sank on October 14 after a fire, but all 21 crew members were rescued safely.

Per verified web-search coverage (iranianuae.ae citing Al Jazeera): some widely viewed videos originated from an Instagram account called Nativora, which describes itself as a creator of fictional stories and imagery using artificial intelligence.
Telltale fabrication signs cited in that coverage: unnatural movement on the water, unusually shaped boxes, distorted/illegible writing, and motionless people aboard moving boats.
The ship's sinking and the dispersal of its containers and cargo in the water are genuine; the widely circulated images of hundreds of iPhones floating or being retrieved are fabricated.
No credible evidence has been published that the vessel was carrying a shipment of iPhones (per that coverage).

Per verified web-search coverage (The Apple Post, citing Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority): GFS Pride sustained damage and a fire before sinking; all 21 crew safely evacuated; a second Singapore-registered ship, GFS Giselle, was struck on October 13–14, suffered hull damage, and reached safe anchorage.

No specific original X post with the viral footage could be verified — the @Telegraph Oct 16 X post ('Iranians recover new iPhones floating in Strait of Hormuz') is referenced via a shortened t.co link whose exact x.com status URL is unrecoverable here, so x_media_url is null rather than a guess.
stories.full_text:
AI-generated videos of Iranians collecting iPhones go viral
Videos claiming to show Iranian fishermen retrieving iPhones and perfumes from a sunken cargo ship went viral online. However, an Al Jazeera investigation found the clips were AI-generated. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sank on October 14 after a fire, but all 21 crew members were rescued safely. The videos reportedly garnered millions of views across social media platforms.
